comments.body:
Root cause proven by controlled probe before any code change. Probe advanced a test execution row from TASK_RECEIVED to IMPLEMENTING via persist_execution_state and observed a byte identical updated_at, confirming the onupdate default does not fire for the on_conflict_do_update set_ mapping. Two competing hypotheses were refuted first. An empty EXECUTION_ORPHAN_GRACE_SECONDS in .env resolves to 120, not 0. The updated_at values are timezone aware UTC and produce clean deltas.

Production evidence: execution intake-ee0f760a reached PR_CREATED at 02:40:46 and was marked CANCELLED at 02:41:19, 33 seconds later against a 120 second grace, because its frozen updated_at was 39 minutes old. That freed the intake active guard and admitted duplicate run intake-8383b6ac for the same ticket.

Each acceptance criterion selector was run on its own and passed. Reverting each fix independently was checked to fail the matching tests, so none of them pass vacuously. Full inv ci is green with 1457 passed, 6 skipped, and eval-gate PASS.

The fix deliberately does not add PR_CREATED to a global terminal state list. services/orchestration/webhook/pr_events.py selects non-terminal executions to resolve which run to signal when a pull request closes, so PR_CREATED has to stay non-terminal there.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body: Classified as regression. The omitted updated_at in the upsert set_ mapping dates to the original schema in ADEVX-1 (3ed3ff9) and was latent and harmless on its own. The orphan reconciler added in ADEVX-95 (b5968c0) started reading that frozen column as an activity timestamp, which is what turned a dormant defect into cancelled successful runs and duplicate admissions.

compiled_state.description:
The orphan reconciler cancels executions that already finished successfully, which starts a duplicate run and breaks close on merge.

Two defects combine. First, persist_execution_state upserts with on_conflict_do_update and an explicit set_ mapping that omits updated_at, so the onupdate default never fires and updated_at freezes at row creation. The reconciler grace window therefore measures age since creation rather than age since activity, so any run lasting longer than the grace is eligible the moment its workflow stops being live. Second, the reconciler treats any non-terminal execution with no live workflow as an orphan, but PR_CREATED and AWAITING_PR_CLOSE are states a successful run reaches after its workflow has legitimately ended while it waits on an external pull request event.

Observed on execution intake-ee0f760a, which reached PR_CREATED at 02:40:46 and was marked CANCELLED at 02:41:19, thirty three seconds later, against a grace of one hundred and twenty seconds. Its frozen updated_at was thirty nine minutes old. Cancelling the row then freed the intake active guard, which admitted a duplicate run for the same ticket. Cancelling it also hides the execution from the pull request webhook lookup in services/orchestration/webhook/pr_events.py, which selects non-terminal executions to signal when the pull request closes, so the ticket would never close on merge.

Fix both. Refresh updated_at in the conflict update so the grace window measures activity. Carry the execution state on ActiveExecution and skip the states that are expected to have no live workflow, leaving genuine orphan reclamation intact.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The execution upsert refreshes updated_at on conflict, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_execution_persistence.py -k upsert_refreshes_updated_at`
- [x] The active execution query selects the state column, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_execution_persistence.py -k active_query_selects_state`
- [x] ActiveExecution carries the execution state, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_execution_reconciler.py -k carries_state`
- [x] The reconciler leaves a PR_CREATED execution alone, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_execution_reconciler.py -k skips_pr_created`
- [x] The reconciler leaves an AWAITING_PR_CLOSE execution alone, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_execution_reconciler.py -k skips_awaiting_pr_close`
- [x] The reconciler still reclaims a dead execution in a working state, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_execution_reconciler.py -k reclaims_dead_working_state`

## Testing
Run `pytest tests/unit/test_execution_persistence.py tests/unit/test_execution_reconciler.py -q` to prove the upsert contract and the reclamation policy, then `ruff check .` for lint.
